note: selector/stamp lifecycle. `resolution` is what a reader does per catalog load (structural validation only); `provenance` is what jawakad alone does at startup and before a ROM scan (full hashing); `publication` and `cleanup` cover the content-addressed publish protocol; `digest` locks the canonical-bytes and tree-hash rules against hand-written literals.

resolution.name: resolves-selected-generation
resolution.note: the ordinary path: both consumers agree on whatever `current` names, and neither of them rehashes a core to get there.

resolution.name: selector-swap
resolution.note: after a swap both readers resolve the NEW generation. A reader already inside the old immutable directory may finish its snapshot; it just never starts a new one there.

resolution.name: selector-missing
resolution.note: the state left behind by invalidation, or by a crash mid-compile. Release defaults, not an error.

resolution.name: selector-malformed-no-newline
resolution.note: the grammar is exact. This value names a directory a reader is about to open, so anything permissive here is a path-handling bug waiting to happen.

resolution.name: selector-malformed-traversal
resolution.note: the reason a strict grammar exists at all.

resolution.name: generation-missing
resolution.note: a valid selector naming a directory that is not there.

resolution.name: generation-incomplete-outputs
resolution.note: the directory exists but cores.json does not. A partially written generation must never be served.

resolution.name: stamp-platform-mismatch
resolution.note: a card moved between devices. The systems list is platform-specific, so this is a fallback, not a warning.

resolution.name: stamp-release-mismatch-after-ota
resolution.note: D2: the post-OTA system list must match the new release exactly. A stale catalog that silently pins a user to a pre-OTA system list is worse than not shipping the feature.

resolution.name: release-identity-unavailable
resolution.note: T-5: release.json missing or unreadable. The compiler never guesses an identity.

resolution.name: release-defaults-invalid
resolution.note: T-4: when BOTH the effective generation and the release defaults fail, the answer is an explicit catalog error. There is no stale-data fallback to reach for.

resolution.name: cs-survives-daemon-restart
resolution.note: T-4: a long-lived CS process outliving a jawakad crash. During the gap the selector is absent, so CS serves release defaults -- never the generation it had cached a moment ago.
resolution.cache_note: CS may cache structural validation only while the exact `current` value and installed release_id are unchanged; both changed here, so the cache is void.

provenance.name: producer-fresh
provenance.note: everything hashes as recorded; no recompile.

provenance.name: producer-base-mismatch
provenance.note: an OTA or a manual drag-the-ZIP replaced the release defaults. base.info_sha256 is in the stamp precisely so a partial manual copy that left release_id alone is still caught.

provenance.name: producer-contributor-mismatch-swapped-so
provenance.note: P1-7: the .so was swapped without touching `provides`. Fingerprinting every DECLARED FILE, not just the manifest, is what catches this -- the compiler's status output asserted that exact file was present and usable.

provenance.name: producer-invalidates-selector-before-recompiling
provenance.note: the ordering is the contract: unlink `current`, fsync, THEN recompile. During the gap every new reader gets release defaults, and a crash mid-compile leaves no selector rather than one pointing at unverified output.

publication.name: identical-generation-reuse
publication.note: T-2: a no-op recompile lands on the same content-addressed name, is verified, and reuses the existing directory. No counter, no garbage, no second copy.

publication.name: generation-digest-conflict
publication.note: the same name holding different bytes is corruption. Fail closed, diagnose it, and do NOT overwrite a directory a reader may be inside.

publication.name: compile-failure-leaves-readable-diagnostics
publication.note: diagnostics.json lives OUTSIDE every generation, so a compile that produced no directory at all still leaves an explanation a developer and the Pak Rat UI can read.

cleanup.name: temp-only-cleanup
cleanup.note: S-4/T-4: v1 removes abandoned temp directories and NOTHING else. Finalized generations persist across daemon restarts because a CS process may still be reading one.

digest.name: canonical-stamp-bytes
digest.note: the exact bytes hashed to name a generation, spelled out by hand. Producer and both readers must agree on this or they disagree about which generation is current.

digest.name: contributor-ordering-is-normative
digest.note: arrays keep their order through canonicalization, so the producer must sort contributors by provider (and each contributor's files by rel) BEFORE hashing. Unsorted input produces a different, wrong digest.

digest.name: tree-hash-length-prefix
digest.note: without the uint64 length prefix, {'a': 'x', 'b': 'yz'} and {'a': 'xy', 'b': 'z'} hash identically -- an .info directory could be rewritten across a file boundary and keep a valid stamp.

digest.name: tree-hash-empty
digest.note: a missing .info directory and an empty one contribute the same nothing, so they hash the same.
